leading_positions.synthesis: All six round-1 configurations are a single-part B027 prize crediting Daniel J. Drucker, Jens Juul Holst and Svetlana Mojsov, with citations that all name GLP-1 physiology and its active form as enabling incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. Shared: the same three names, the same single-achievement framing, and the same case (a complete chain from mechanism to patient benefit, large independent outcome trials, no maturity concern). Not shared: citation wording differs slightly (some say 'active form', one says 'molecular identity', one frames it as 'the incretin principle'), and every member still records Lotte Bjerre Knudsen and uncredited early contributors such as Joel Habener as unresolved attribution risks. The chair's opening trio included Knudsen in the third seat; the chair now supports Mojsov in that seat.

areas_of_agreement: All six members place B027 first and propose the identical trio Drucker, Holst and Mojsov in round 1; none proposes a second prize part.

All six state that unanimity of opening rank is not itself the argument and rest the case on the mechanism-to-patient chain, independent replication in large randomized trials, and stable interpretation after decades.

All six name attribution as the strongest reservation against B027, specifically the exclusion of Knudsen and the unverified priority position of Habener and other early contributors outside the supplied credit list.
No member discloses a conflict with any shortlisted candidate or credited name; several note co-authorship among committee members or shared Karolinska affiliation without link to any candidate.
Several members (El-Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann, Wahren-Herlenius) place B025 or B035 among their alternatives, and members who comment on B035 and B025 agree that each has an attribution problem.
scientific_disputes: Whether B027 honours the physiology and molecular identity of GLP-1 (Holst, Mojsov, Drucker) or the path to the medicines, which would bring in Knudsen's long-acting analogue engineering; members describe this as the only substantive disagreement within B027, and the round-1 files record all six now favouring the physiology reading.

Whether clinical consequence or mechanistic originality should weigh more for the second-tier candidates: B020 (cGAS-STING) is described by Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius as mechanistically clean but by Perlmann, El-Manira and Wahren-Herlenius as lacking a delivered therapy, while B025 is valued for its patient record.

Whether a methodological tool (B035 optogenetics) can rank alongside a physiological discovery with measured patient benefit; Linnarsson ranks it above CAR-T for originality and breadth, El-Manira, Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius rank it lower because it is a tool with early clinical use.

Whether B043 (unfolded protein response) and B004 (orexin) have enough direct disease consequence to stand beside B027; Sandberg values B043 for clean credit and maturity, while others call its disease link indirect, and the autoimmune etiology of narcolepsy is noted as incompletely resolved.
attribution_disputes: B027 third seat: Mojsov versus Knudsen. Four credited names compete for three seats, and each member's file records this tension.

Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36)/(7-37) peptide relative to the Habener group, which is not in the supplied credit list, is flagged as unverified by Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg, Wahren-Herlenius, El-Manira and the chair.

B025 (CAR-T): the credited names June, Sadelain and Rosenberg describe costimulation, clinical translation and adoptive transfer as distinct strands, and the earlier chimeric-receptor concept (Eshhar and others) is outside the credit list; flagged by El-Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann and Wahren-Herlenius.

B035 (optogenetics): six credited names split between channel discovery and characterisation (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and neuronal deployment (Deisseroth, Boyden, Miesenboeck); any three-person set excludes someone with a documented claim.

B020 (cGAS-STING): the Chen and Barber pairing is described as the cleanest on the list, but Ishikawa, Sun, Wu and the cyclic dinucleotide precedent (Vance, Burdette) raise unresolved priority questions.

B011 (TOR): Wahren-Herlenius's single-name Hall proposal avoids the Sabatini and Schreiber questions but, per Linnarsson, Perlmann and Sandberg, leaves out the rapamycin-FKBP12 target and mTORC1 nutrient-sensing chain.
maturity_disputes: B027 is judged mature by all six members, with no maturity objection recorded.

B020: therapeutic validation of STING agonists or inhibitors is pending; Perlmann, Wahren-Herlenius and El-Manira treat this as a limit on a prize this year, while Sandberg and the chair treat the mechanism as already mature.
B035: clinical translation (for example vision restoration) is described as early by El-Manira, Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius.
B025: efficacy is so far confined mainly to haematological cancers, with open questions on solid tumours, toxicity and durability, as noted by Perlmann and Wahren-Herlenius.
B004: members differ on whether the disease mechanism is settled enough, given the unresolved autoimmune etiology of human narcolepsy.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: No member records a conflict with any shortlisted candidate or credited name, and none requests recusal.

Disclosed relationships among committee members, treated as context only and not linked to any candidate: the chair and Perlmann have about twenty co-authored works, Linnarsson and Sandberg have eight, El-Manira has a co-authored 2009 paper with Perlmann, and Perlmann reports co-authorship with the chair and once with El-Manira.

The chair's Greengard postdoctoral training is disclosed and involves no shortlisted candidate; Sandberg notes IRE1-mediated RNA splicing is close to his RNA-processing interests without any personal tie to the B043 credit list.
questions_for_round2: For B027, does the Committee define the achievement as GLP-1 physiology and molecular identity (Drucker, Holst, Mojsov) or as incretin-based therapy (which would bring Knudsen into the third seat), and what exact citation wording follows from that choice?

What evidence in the supplied materials, if any, can settle Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide relative to Habener and other uncredited early contributors, and if it cannot be settled, does that change the Mojsov-or-Knudsen decision?

Is a second part worth the cost of reducing the B027 trio, given that El-Manira, Perlmann, Sandberg and the chair lean toward a single-achievement prize while Perlmann, Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius would consider pairing a second part on merit; if a second part is wanted, which of B035, B025, B020 or B043 and with how many names?

If B027 were set aside or judged too contested, which fallback does the Committee prefer, B025 (Wahren-Herlenius, Linnarsson, El-Manira), B035 (Linnarsson, El-Manira, the chair), B020 (Sandberg, Perlmann, Wahren-Herlenius) or another, and can the Eshhar, Bamberg-Boyden-Miesenboeck or Ishikawa-Sun-Wu attribution problems be resolved within three names?

How should the Committee weigh mechanistic clarity with pending therapy (B020, B043) against demonstrated patient benefit (B025), and does maturity require a delivered clinical outcome for a discovery prize?
Would the Committee consider a narrower credit for B011 (Hall alone) viable, given the concern that it omits the mammalian mTOR and rapamycin-target chain?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows complete convergence on B027 with an identical three-name configuration, so the remaining work is to test the Mojsov and Knudsen boundary and the citation wording, not to choose a leading candidate. Support for a second part or a fallback is divided and rests on attribution rather than on disagreement about the underlying science. Because opening unanimity can conceal different readings of what is being honoured, round 2 should state those readings explicitly. As chair I moved from an opening trio including Knudsen to the physiology trio after hearing colleagues, and this is disclosed so that it is not mistaken for independent confirmation.
